sources.entry: FotoApta - Generates professional AI portraits from one selfie, with a free watermarked preview and an optional one-time HD pack. #freemium

summary.name: FotoApta AI Headshot
summary.one_liner: A web service that turns one selfie into six AI-generated professional headshots (suit, blazer, business shirt) for LinkedIn or résumés, with a free watermarked preview and a $9.99 one-time paid pack.
use_cases: Create a LinkedIn profile photo from a selfie
Make a résumé headshot without a photographer
Generate business photos in suit or blazer
Get multiple background options for a profile photo
summary.what_it_does: The service takes one front-facing, well-lit selfie (JPG, PNG or WebP, up to 8 MB) and generates a free preview, limited to 3 attempts per day per network. A paid one-time pack for $9.99 produces six high-resolution headshots without watermark, in suit, blazer and business shirt looks on grey, white and beige backdrops. The page says it aims to preserve the person's identity while changing clothing and background, but AI can alter details, so every result should be reviewed. Previews can take around 2 minutes. The page states the images are produced by API-called models (Qwen-Image-Edit for previews; Seedream with Wanx fallback for paid photos), not run on the company's own infrastructure.
notable: Free watermarked preview with no account or card required, then optional $9.99 one-time pack of 6 HD photos
Explicitly not valid for passports, visas or official documents; points to separate in-browser ID photo tools
Discloses underlying models: Qwen-Image-Edit for previews, Seedream (ByteDance) with Wanx (Alibaba) fallback for paid photos
Selfies are sent to third-party providers; service says it does not store them in its database and does not train models on user photos
caveats: Official documents such as passports and visas do not accept these AI-generated photos
Free previews are limited to 3 per day and share a network-wide and service-wide daily cap; paid pack is required for no-watermark results
AI may alter facial details, so results need manual review; refund terms are only in the terms of use
